node.title: Re: Comparing string hex / korean (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Assuming the hex string isrepresents UTF-8, you could do this:

use warnings; use strict; use open qw/:std :utf8/; use HTML::Entities qw/decode_entities/; my $x = '리작'; my $xd = decode_entities($x); my $y = '\\xeb\\xa6\\xac\\xec\\x9e\\x91'; (my $yd = $y) =~ s/\\x([0-9a-f]{2})/chr hex $1/eig; utf8::decode($yd); print "$x =>$xd<=\n"; print "$y =>$yd<=\n"; if ( $xd eq $yd ) { print "Match!\n" } else { die "Mismatch!\n" }

Output:

리작 =>리작<=
\xeb\xa6\xac\xec\x9e\x91 =>리작<=
Match!

Update: I realized it's unclear to me whether your original string was player=리작 or player=리작 - the latter happens on PerlMonks when you put Unicode characters into tags. You'd have to use 

 or  tags instead, but then characters that have special meanings (either as HTML or by the PerlMonks engine) have to be escaped, such as <=>, &=&, [=[, etc. If your original string was player=리작, then you don't need the decode_entities step - but it is necessary for the input string in $cfg{'default.player'} to have been properly decoded first though (you can check this e.g. with [doc://Devel::Peek], [id://1227736|see also]).
